raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, and on just 2.2 mu I can’t afford to gamble. Same as most years, I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation because that’s the safest way for my land and for our household. I only finished primary school, so I don’t go by fancy formulas. I look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and whether I can afford the inputs. Wheat still needs proper base fertilizer and a topdress, otherwise the stand gets weak. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, fast, with simple land prep because the turnaround is tight. I have a well, so if the rain doesn’t come, I’ll irrigate wheat a few times because wheat is more sensitive here. Maize I’ll water less, only if it turns dry at a key stage. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, but with such a small plot and only two people at home, I still keep everything modest and practical.
